articles.title: 100 Years of Lufthansa: Seven People Who Shaped Our History
articles.description: In our 100-year history, there have been many formative events and successes: spectacular long-distance flights in the early years, new aircraft types, technical innovations, and ever-increasing comfort on board. All of this has been made possible by people. Meet seven of them who paved the way and shaped Lufthansa into the iconic airline it is today
articles.image-alt: A smiling pilot wearing goggles and a flight cap waves from an aircraft decorated with a floral wreath.
articles.author: Lufthansa Editorial Team

articles.title: “Everyone wants to fly with the cranes”
articles.description: The crane symbolizes longing and wanderlust, which is one of the reasons it has always been featured on Lufthansa aircraft. To protect this migratory bird, Lufthansa works closely with Crane Protection Germany. Volunteer crane ranger Hildegard Lamberty and Dr. Günter Nowald, director of the NABU Crane Center in Vorpommern, explain what makes these animals so special
articles.image-alt: A flock of six cranes flying across a clear blue sky
articles.author: Interview: Aileen Tiedemann

articles.title: Lufthansa in the Spotlight
articles.description: Gold records, Hollywood film shoots, famous passengers, and its own orchestra: the Lufthansa brand has been shaping pop culture for decades
articles.image-alt: A concert in a glamorous theater hall with a band, orchestra, spotlights, and confetti
articles.author: 100 years Lufthansa

articles.title: Welcome to My World: Elyas M’Barek
articles.description: Elyas M’Barek’s new film is called “Der perfekte Urlaub” (“The Perfect Vacation”) and was shot in Mallorca, but in his free time, the actor prefers to go kitesurfing in the Caribbean or take a city break in Japan. M’Barek spoke with Lufthansa Insights about his travel experiences and the three years he spent living in New York

articles.author: Interview: Aileen Tiedemann
